A database administrator is responsible for keeping data safe and available. Daily tasks include creating user accounts, giving each user only the rights needed, and taking regular backups. A backup is useful only if it can be restored, so the administrator tests restores from time to time. When a query runs slowly, the administrator checks whether an index is missing before buying faster hardware. Good records of every change help the team find the cause when something goes wrong.
questions.question: Why does the administrator test restores?
options: A backup is useful only if it can be restored.
questions.explanation: The passage says a backup is useful only if it can be restored.

questions.passage:
**Read the passage and answer the next 5 questions.**
Public Wi-Fi is convenient, but it is often not safe. Anyone on the same network may be able to watch the data that passes through it, unless the website uses encryption. Banking and email should therefore be avoided on open networks. A virtual private network (VPN) encrypts the traffic between a device and a trusted server, which protects the user even on a shared network. Turning off automatic connection to open networks is also a simple step.
questions.question: Why should banking be avoided on open Wi-Fi?
options: Others on the network may watch unencrypted data.
questions.explanation: The passage says anyone on the same network may watch the data unless it is encrypted.
